newsitem.title: USA: Los Angeles council to vote on $200 mln arena plan.
newsitem.headline: Los Angeles council to vote on $200 mln arena plan.

text.p: The Los Angeles City Council on Friday will vote on a controversial plan to build a $200 million sports and entertainment complex in the downtown area.
Friday's vote on the memorandum of understanding will cap months of negotiations over the proposed arena development for the Los Angeles Kings hockey team and the Lakers basketball team.
In January, the city council tentatively approved the proposal by a vote of 13-two.

Under the proposal, the city would contribute about $70 million to the project. The city's contribution would be funded with a taxable debt financing of $50.5 million and $20 million from a bond reserve fund. The average annual cost of the city's contribution was estimated to be $6.8 million.

The city's contribution would be fully recovered from tax revenues generated by the arena and from other sources, city negotiators said. Developers have agreed to levy a special surcharge on arena tickets to help the city pay off the bonds.
City negotiators maintain the transaction would bolster the downtown economy by creating jobs. Critics of the plan say it would put city taxpayers at risk.
